artists.desc: Seattle psych-folk band led by singer-songwriter Peter Sumic, recording since 2015 with a rotating lineup. Their guitar-driven psychedelic rock mixes in garage rock, folk rock and organ-led pop, recorded to analogue tape. They tour the Northwest steadily, which is consistent with a Shelton club date.

artists.name: Hoodstock Finale
artists.desc: Hoodstock festival session. It is a nonprofit benefit supporting youth music and environmental education. Official site: https://www.hoodstock.org/

artists.name: Josh Meeks
artists.desc: Mason County performer who appears solo under his own name and also fronts the band Maid Marion.

artists.name: Kitty Mae
artists.desc: Country singer-songwriter and guitarist who bills herself as the Cascade Cowgirl. Born and raised in Washington, she started out singing the national anthem at fairs and rodeos and busking at Pike Place Market, and now plays across western Washington. Her sound blends classic country storytelling with modern country rock, drawing on Dolly Parton, Miranda Lambert, Gretchen Wilson and The Chicks. A two-time Northwest CMA award winner, including Favorite Local Act of 2024.

artists.name: Maid Marion
artists.desc: Maid Marion is Josh Meeks performing with other musicians backing him. He also plays solo under his own name around Mason County.

artists.name: Open Mic
artists.desc: Recurring open-mic night, not a performer. Weekly patterns in the data: Taylor Station on Wednesdays, 2 Margaritas on Mondays, Hood Canalé on Thursdays.

artists.name: Sammy Steele
artists.home: North Dakota-born, Pacific Northwest-raised; now splits time between the Northwest and Wyoming
artists.desc: Singer-songwriter with a gravelly baritone working in the outlaw country tradition of Merle Haggard, Waylon Jennings and Johnny Cash, mixed with the 90s country he grew up on and a streak of southern and alternative rock. He began performing at open mics after moving to Las Vegas in 2005, then returned to the Northwest and built a following across Washington, Oregon, Idaho and Montana. He plays Shelton regularly, including full-band shows at Little Creek Casino.

artists.name: Scott Lesman Duo
artists.desc: Two-piece act led by Union-based musician Scott Lesman, described by Hood Canalé as two musicians playing anything from Motown to classic rock along with a good deal of their own original material. Scott Lesman is listed as a musician member of the North Mason Chamber of Commerce in Union, and the duo plays regularly around Hood Canal and the Kitsap Peninsula.

artists.name: Suped Up Fjord
artists.desc: Cover band based in Union that describes itself as playing "both kinds of music, rock and roll." They perform as a duo, trio or full band depending on the venue, and play regularly around Mason County including local festivals. The trio configuration is billed as the "Fjord Piece Trio."

artists.name: The Lady Drinks Whiskey
artists.desc: Local cover band playing classic rock and blues, made up of Pam Wiley on vocals, Scott Taylor on guitar and vocals, and Mike Burdorff on guitar, mandolin, harmonica and vocals. Their repertoire spans the Beatles and Beach Boys through Janis Joplin, Elvis and Willie Nelson. They play small venues and private parties across the Puget Sound region and appear regularly at Hood Canal venues.

artists.name: The Shoemaker Brothers
artists.home: Originally Shelton & Mason County, WA; later based in Los Angeles, CA
artists.desc: A band of four brothers — Samuel, Nathanael, Daniel and Gabriel Shoemaker — who grew up in Mason County and were classically trained on strings before forming the band in the mid-2000s. They play original folk and rockabilly-tinged rock, swapping instruments mid-song, and have toured nationally after relocating to Los Angeles. A Mason County homecoming appearance explains the sold-out Hoodstock billing.
